title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 14. The Marriage of Sri Vishnupriya
html:
Moved by Sanatana's grief, the Lord consents to the wedding; the adhivasa of bridegroom and bride; the wedding procession and the rite in Sanatana's house; Shachi welcomes the couple home

Verse 1

ततश्च भगवान्कृष्णः करुणापरमानसः।
तयोर्दुःखमनुस्मृत्य प्रापय्य निजब्राह्मणम्॥१॥

tataśca bhagavānkṛṣṇaḥ karuṇāparamānasaḥ|
tayorduḥkhamanusmṛtya prāpayya nijabrāhmaṇam||1||

tatah — then; cha — and; bhagavan — Bhagavan; krishnah — Krishna; karuna-para-manasah — His heart intent on compassion; tayoh — their; duhkham — sorrow; anusmritya — remembering; prapayya — sending; nija-brahmanam — His own brahmana.

1Then Bhagavan Krishna, whose heart is devoted to compassion, remembered their sorrow and sent His own brahmana to them,

Verse 2

वाण्या मधुरया विप्रमुखेन प्राकृतो यथा।
अनुनीय तयोः कन्यामुद्वाहार्थं मनो दधे॥२॥

vāṇyā madhurayā vipramukhena prākṛto yathā|
anunīya tayoḥ kanyāmudvāhārthaṁ mano dadhe||2||

vanya madhuraya — with sweet words; vipra-mukhena — through the mouth of the brahmana; prakritah — an ordinary man; yatha — like; anuniya — having conciliated (them); tayoh — their; kanyam — daughter; udvaha-artham — to marry; manah — mind; dadhe — He set.

2and, like an ordinary man, He conciliated them with sweet words through the mouth of that brahmana and resolved to marry their daughter.

Verse 3

ततः शुभे विलग्नेन्दुनक्षत्रशुभसंयुते।
अधिवासदिने साधुविप्रसङ्घसमागते॥३॥

tataḥ śubhe vilagnendunakṣatraśubhasaṁyute|
adhivāsadine sādhuviprasaṅghasamāgate||3||

tatah — then; shubhe — on the auspicious; vilagna-indu-nakshatra-shubha-samyute — marked by a favourable conjunction of the lagna, the moon and the nakshatra; adhivasa-dine — on the day of the adhivasa; sadhu-vipra-sangha-samagate — when hosts of saintly brahmanas had gathered.

3And so came the auspicious day of the adhivasa, marked by a favourable conjunction of the lagna, the moon and the nakshatra1. Hosts of saintly brahmanas gathered,

Verse 4

मृदङ्गपणवाध्माने वेदध्वनिनिनादिते।
धूपदीपपताकाभिरलङ्कृतदिगन्तरे॥४॥

mṛdaṅgapaṇavādhmāne vedadhvanininādite|
dhūpadīpapatākābhiralaṅkṛtadigantare||4||

mridanga-panava-adhmane — when mridangas and panavas resounded; veda-dhvani-ninadite — ringing with the sound of the Vedas; dhupa-dipa-patakabhih — with incense, lamps and banners; alankrita-dik-antare — when all quarters were adorned.

4mridangas and panavas resounded, everything rang with the sound of the Vedas, and all the quarters were adorned with incense, lamps and banners.

Verse 5

स्वस्तिवाचनपूर्वं हि सम्पूज्य पितृदेवताः।
अधिवासक्रियां चक्रे ब्राह्मणैः सह स प्रभुः॥५॥

svastivācanapūrvaṁ hi sampūjya pitṛdevatāḥ|
adhivāsakriyāṁ cakre brāhmaṇaiḥ saha sa prabhuḥ||5||

svasti-vachana-purvam — preceded by the recitation of blessings (svasti-vachana); hi — indeed; sampujya — having worshipped; pitri-devatah — the forefathers and the gods; adhivasa-kriyam — the rite of adhivasa; chakre — performed; brahmanaih saha — together with the brahmanas; sah — that; prabhuh — Prabhu.

5After the recitation of blessings and the worship of the forefathers and the gods, Prabhu performed the rite of adhivasa together with the brahmanas.

Verse 6

ततो ददौ द्विजातिभ्यः सज्जनेभ्यश्च चन्दनम्।
गन्धताम्बूलमाल्यं च भूरि भूरियशा हरिः॥६॥

tato dadau dvijātibhyaḥ sajjanebhyaśca candanam|
gandhatāmbūlamālyaṁ ca bhūri bhūriyaśā hariḥ||6||

tatah — then; dadau — gave; dvijatibhyah — to the twice-born; sajjanebhyah — to the good people; cha — and; chandanam — sandal paste; gandha-tambula-malyam — perfumes, betel and garlands; cha — and; bhuri — abundantly; bhuri-yashah — of great fame; harih — Hari.

6Then Hari of great fame lavishly presented the twice-born and the good people with sandal paste, perfumes, betel2 and garlands.

Verse 7

तस्मिन्काले पण्डितार्यः श्रीयुतः श्रीसनातनः।
अभ्ययाच्छ्रद्धया युक्तः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥७॥

tasminkāle paṇḍitāryaḥ śrīyutaḥ śrīsanātanaḥ|
abhyayācchraddhayā yuktaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā||7||

tasmin kale — at that time; pandita-aryah — the noble pandita; shri-yutah — the venerable; shri-sanatanah — Sri Sanatana; abhyayat — came; shraddhaya yuktah — full of reverence; prahrishtena antar-atmana — with a rejoicing heart.

7At that time the venerable Sri Sanatana, the noble pandita, arrived, full of reverence, his heart rejoicing.

Verse 8

ब्राह्मणान्विप्रसाध्वीश्च प्रेषयित्वा यथाविधि।
कारयामास जामातुरधिवासं महात्मनः॥८॥

brāhmaṇānviprasādhvīśca preṣayitvā yathāvidhi|
kārayāmāsa jāmāturadhivāsaṁ mahātmanaḥ||8||

brahmanan — brahmanas; vipra-sadhvih — virtuous brahmana wives; cha — and; preshayitva — sending; yatha-vidhi — according to the rite; karayam asa — had performed; jamatuh — of his son-in-law; adhivasam — the adhivasa; maha-atmanah — high-souled.

8He sent brahmanas and virtuous brahmana wives and had the adhivasa of his high-souled son-in-law performed according to the rite,

Verse 9

स्वयं चक्रे स्वदुहितुरधिवासं यथाविधि।
महानन्दरसे मग्नो नाविन्दद्भववेदनाम्॥९॥

svayaṁ cakre svaduhituradhivāsaṁ yathāvidhi|
mahānandarase magno nāvindadbhavavedanām||9||

svayam — himself; chakre — performed; sva-duhituh — of his own daughter; adhivasam — the adhivasa; yatha-vidhi — according to the rite; maha-ananda-rase — in the rapture of great joy; magnah — immersed; na — not; avindat — felt; bhava-vedanam — the pains of worldly existence.

9while he himself performed his daughter's adhivasa according to the rite and, immersed in the rapture of great joy, felt nothing of the pains of worldly existence.

Verse 10

अथापरदिने प्रातर्भगवाञ्जाह्नवीजलम्।
अवगाह्याह्निकं कृत्वा प्रायात्साधुभिरन्वितः॥१०॥

athāparadine prātarbhagavāñjāhnavījalam|
avagāhyāhnikaṁ kṛtvā prāyātsādhubhiranvitaḥ||10||

atha — then; apara-dine — on the next day; pratah — in the morning; bhagavan — Bhagavan; jahnavi-jalam — into the waters of the Jahnavi; avagahya — plunging; ahnikam — the daily rites; kritva — performing; prayat — set out; sadhubhih anvitah — accompanied by saintly men.

10The next morning Bhagavan, having bathed in the waters of the Jahnavi and performed His daily rites, went on His way accompanied by saintly men.

Verse 11

नान्दीमुखान्पितृगणान्सम्पूज्य सुसमाहितः।
स्थितं तं सहसाभ्येत्य द्विजपुत्रा महौजसः॥११॥

nāndīmukhānpitṛgaṇānsampūjya susamāhitaḥ|
sthitaṁ taṁ sahasābhyetya dvijaputrā mahaujasaḥ||11||

nandimukhan — the nandimukha; pitri-ganan — hosts of forefathers; sampujya — having worshipped; su-samahitah — with full attention; sthitam — seated; tam — Him; sahasa — at once; abhyetya — approaching; dvija-putrah — sons of brahmanas; maha-ojasah — full of vigour.

11When, having attentively worshipped the forefathers with the nandimukha rite3, He was seated, vigorous young sons of brahmanas at once approached Him

Verse 12

वस्त्रालङ्कारमालाभिर्गन्धाद्यैः समभूषयन्।
श्रीमद्विश्वम्भरं देवं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम्॥१२॥

vastrālaṅkāramālābhirgandhādyaiḥ samabhūṣayan|
śrīmadviśvambharaṁ devaṁ sūryakoṭisamaprabham||12||

vastra-alankara-malabhih — with garments, ornaments and garlands; gandha-adyaih — with perfumes and the rest; samabhushayan — they adorned; shrimat-vishvambharam — Srimad Vishvambhara; devam — the Lord; surya-koti-sama-prabham — radiant as millions of suns.

12and adorned Srimad Vishvambhara, the Lord radiant as millions of suns, with garments, ornaments and garlands, perfumes and the rest.

Verse 13

तस्मिन्क्षणे चकाराशु श्रीसनातनपण्डितः।
वस्त्रालङ्कारमालाभिर्गन्धाद्यैः समलङ्कृताम्॥१३॥

tasminkṣaṇe cakārāśu śrīsanātanapaṇḍitaḥ|
vastrālaṅkāramālābhirgandhādyaiḥ samalaṅkṛtām||13||

tasmin kshane — at that moment; chakara — made; ashu — quickly; shri-sanatana-panditah — Sri Sanatana Pandita; vastra-alankara-malabhih — with garments, ornaments and garlands; gandha-adyaih — with perfumes and the rest; samalankritam — adorned.

13At that very moment Sri Sanatana Pandita quickly had his daughter adorned with garments, ornaments, garlands, perfumes and the rest,

Verse 14

कन्यां वैवाहिकं कालं विदित्वा ब्राह्मणोत्तमान्।
प्रेषयामास जामातुरादरानयनाय सः॥१४॥

kanyāṁ vaivāhikaṁ kālaṁ viditvā brāhmaṇottamān|
preṣayāmāsa jāmāturādarānayanāya saḥ||14||

kanyam — his daughter; vaivahikam — for the wedding; kalam — the time; viditva — knowing; brahmana-uttaman — excellent brahmanas; preshayam asa — sent; jamatuh — of the son-in-law; adara-anayanaya — to bring with honour; sah — he.

14and, knowing that the hour of the wedding had come, sent excellent brahmanas to bring his son-in-law with honour.

Verse 15

ततो गत्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठाः प्रोचुश्च विनयान्विताः।
उद्वाहार्थं तव शुभः कालोऽयं समुपस्थितः॥१५॥

tato gatvā dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ procuśca vinayānvitāḥ|
udvāhārthaṁ tava śubhaḥ kālo'yaṁ samupasthitaḥ||15||

tatah — then; gatva — going; dvija-shreshthah — the best of brahmanas; prochuh — said; cha — and; vinaya-anvitah — humbly; udvaha-artham — for the wedding; tava — Your; shubhah — auspicious; kalah — time; ayam — this; samupasthitah — has arrived.

15Arriving, those best of brahmanas humbly said: "The auspicious hour of Your wedding has come.

Verse 16

विजयस्व शुभाय त्वं गमनाय मतिं कुरु।
पण्डितस्य गृहे तस्य भाग्यं को वक्तुमर्हति॥१६॥

vijayasva śubhāya tvaṁ gamanāya matiṁ kuru|
paṇḍitasya gṛhe tasya bhāgyaṁ ko vaktumarhati||16||

vijayasva — set forth in triumph; shubhaya — for the auspicious (rite); tvam — You; gamanaya — to going; matim — mind; kuru — turn; panditasya — of the pandita; grihe — to the house; tasya — his; bhagyam — good fortune; kah — who; vaktum — to describe; arhati — can.

16Set forth in triumph on this auspicious errand, make up Your mind to go to the pandita's house! Who can describe his good fortune?"

Verse 17

तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणवचो भगवान्सादराननः।
जयघोषैर्ब्रह्मघोषैर्मृदङ्गपटहस्वनैः॥१७॥

tacchrutvā brāhmaṇavaco bhagavānsādarānanaḥ|
jayaghoṣairbrahmaghoṣairmṛdaṅgapaṭahasvanaiḥ||17||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; brahmana-vachah — the words of the brahmanas; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sa-adara-ananah — with a gracious face; jaya-ghoshaih — with cries of "jaya!"; brahma-ghoshaih — with the chanting of the Vedas; mridanga-pataha-svanaih — with the sound of mridangas and patahas.

17Hearing the words of the brahmanas, Bhagavan smiled graciously4, at once bowed to His mother, mounted a palanquin and joyfully set out amid cries of "jaya!", the chanting of the Vedas, the sound of mridangas and patahas,

Verse 18

वीणापणवकांस्यादिनिस्वनैर्मुदितो ययौ।
मातरं सम्प्रणम्याशु दोलारोहणपूर्वकम्॥१८॥

vīṇāpaṇavakāṁsyādinisvanairmudito yayau|
mātaraṁ sampraṇamyāśu dolārohaṇapūrvakam||18||

vina-panava-kamsya-adi-nisvanaih — with the sounds of vinas, panavas, bronze cymbals and the rest; muditah — joyful; yayau — went; mataram — to His mother; sampranamya — bowing; ashu — at once; dola-arohana-purvakam — having mounted a litter.

18and the music of vinas, panavas, bronze cymbals and the rest.

Verse 19

दीपावलिभिरन्यैश्च नक्षत्रैरिव चन्द्रमाः।
शरच्चन्द्रांशुशुभ्रायां शिविकायां रराज सः॥१९॥

dīpāvalibhiranyaiśca nakṣatrairiva candramāḥ|
śaraccandrāṁśuśubhrāyāṁ śivikāyāṁ rarāja saḥ||19||

dipa-avalibhih — by rows of lamps; anyaih — by other (lights); cha — and; nakshatraih — by stars; iva — like; chandramah — the moon; sharat-chandra-amshu-shubhrayam — white as the rays of the autumn moon; shibikayam — in the palanquin; raraja — shone; sah — He.

19Surrounded by rows of lamps and other lights, like the moon among the stars, He shone in a palanquin white as the rays of the autumn moon:

Verse 20

सुवर्णगौरः क्षीराब्धौ मेरुशृङ्ग इवापरः।
जगन्मोहनलावण्यं व्यक्तीकृत्य स्वयं हरिः॥२०॥

suvarṇagauraḥ kṣīrābdhau meruśṛṅga ivāparaḥ|
jaganmohanalāvaṇyaṁ vyaktīkṛtya svayaṁ hariḥ||20||

suvarna-gaurah — golden-hued; kshirabdhau — in the Milk Ocean; meru-shringah — a peak of Meru; iva — like; aparah — another; jagat-mohana-lavanyam — world-enchanting beauty; vyaktikritya — revealing; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari.

20golden-hued, like a second peak of Meru in the Milk Ocean, Hari Himself revealed a beauty that enchants the world.

Verse 21

प्राप्तं जामातरं वीक्ष्य हर्षोत्फुल्लतनूरुहः।
उद्यम्यानीय विधिना पाद्यमासनमादरात्॥२१॥

prāptaṁ jāmātaraṁ vīkṣya harṣotphullatanūruhaḥ|
udyamyānīya vidhinā pādyamāsanamādarāt||21||

praptam — arrived; jamataram — the son-in-law; vikshya — seeing; harsha-utphulla-tanuruhah — his hair standing on end with joy; udyamya — rising up; aniya — bringing (Him) in; vidhina — according to the rite; padyam — water for the feet; asanam — a seat; adarat — respectfully.

21Seeing that his son-in-law had arrived, (Sanatana,) his hair standing on end with joy, rose, brought Him in with honour, offered Him according to the rite water for His feet and a seat,

Verse 22

दत्त्वा तं वरयामास वस्त्रस्रगनुलेपनैः।
द्रुतकाञ्चनगौराङ्गं मालतीमाल्यवक्षसम्॥२२॥

dattvā taṁ varayāmāsa vastrasraganulepanaiḥ|
drutakāñcanagaurāṅgaṁ mālatīmālyavakṣasam||22||

dattva — having given; tam — Him; varayam asa — honoured as the bridegroom; vastra-srak-anulepanaih — with garments, garlands and unguents; druta-kanchana-gaura-angam — whose limbs were golden like molten gold; malati-malya-vakshasam — with a garland of malati flowers on His chest.

22and honoured Him as the bridegroom with garments, garlands and unguents. His body was golden like molten gold, and on His chest lay a garland of malati flowers —

Verse 23

मेरुशृङ्गं यथा गङ्गाद्विधाधारासमन्वितम्।
उद्यत्पूर्णनिशानाथवदनं पङ्कजेक्षणम्॥२३॥

meruśṛṅgaṁ yathā gaṅgādvidhādhārāsamanvitam|
udyatpūrṇaniśānāthavadanaṁ paṅkajekṣaṇam||23||

meru-shringam — the peak of Meru; yatha — like; ganga-dvidha-dhara-samanvitam — with the twofold stream of the Ganga; udyat-purna-nisha-natha-vadanam — whose face was like the rising full moon; pankaja-ikshanam — lotus-eyed.

23like the peak of Meru down which the Ganga flows in a twofold stream. His face was like the rising full moon, His eyes like lotuses.

Verse 24

दृष्ट्वा जामातरं श्वश्रूर्मुमोद सुस्मितानना।
सा दीपैः स्वस्तिकैर्लाजैर्माङ्गल्यैस्तद्द्विजस्त्रियः॥२४॥

dṛṣṭvā jāmātaraṁ śvaśrūrmumoda susmitānanā|
sā dīpaiḥ svastikairlājairmāṅgalyaistaddvijastriyaḥ||24||

drishtva — seeing; jamataram — the son-in-law; shvashruh — the mother-in-law; mumoda — rejoiced; su-smita-anana — with a bright smile on her face; sa — she; dipaih — with lamps; svastikaih — with svastikas; lajaih — with parched rice; mangalyaih — with auspicious (things); tat-dvija-striyah — and the brahmana women there.

24Seeing her son-in-law, the mother-in-law rejoiced, her face bright with a smile. She and the brahmana women gathered there — with lamps, svastikas, parched rice and other auspicious things —

Verse 25

चक्रुर्निर्मञ्छनं प्रीता जामातुर्हृद्यकोविदाः।
परमानन्दसम्पूर्णाः कौतूहलसमन्विताः॥२५॥

cakrurnirmañchanaṁ prītā jāmāturhṛdyakovidāḥ|
paramānandasampūrṇāḥ kautūhalasamanvitāḥ||25||

chakruh — performed; nirmanchhanam — the nirmanchhana (waving of auspicious things); pritah — delighted; jamatuh — for the son-in-law; hridya-kovidah — knowing what pleases the heart; parama-ananda-sampurnah — filled with supreme joy; kautuhala-samanvitah — full of eager delight.

25joyfully performed the nirmanchhana rite5 over the son-in-law: filled with supreme bliss and eager delight, they knew well what pleases the heart.

Verse 26

समानीय सुतां दिव्यां श्रीसनातनपण्डितः।
न्यवेदयत्पादमूले जामातुः सुसमाहितः॥२६॥

samānīya sutāṁ divyāṁ śrīsanātanapaṇḍitaḥ|
nyavedayatpādamūle jāmātuḥ susamāhitaḥ||26||

samaniya — bringing; sutam — his daughter; divyam — divine; shri-sanatana-panditah — Sri Sanatana Pandita; nyavedayat — offered; pada-mule — at the feet; jamatuh — of his son-in-law; su-samahitah — with full attention.

26Sri Sanatana Pandita brought his divine daughter and with full attention offered her at the feet of his son-in-law.

Verse 27

ततो जयजयैर्नादैर्विप्राणां वेदनिस्वनैः।
नानावादित्रनिर्घोषैर्बभूव महदुत्सवः॥२७॥

tato jayajayairnādairviprāṇāṁ vedanisvanaiḥ|
nānāvāditranirghoṣairbabhūva mahadutsavaḥ||27||

tatah — then; jaya-jayaih — of "jaya, jaya!"; nadaih — with cries; vipranam — of the brahmanas; veda-nisvanaih — with the sound of the Vedas; nana-vaditra-nirghoshaih — with the din of many instruments; babhuva — there was; mahat — a great; utsavah — festival.

27Then, amid cries of "jaya, jaya!", the sound of the Vedas from the brahmanas' lips and the din of many instruments, a great festival began.

Verse 28

ववर्ष पुष्पैरन्योन्यं विष्णुर्विष्णुप्रिया च सा।
साक्षादेव महानन्दोऽवततार स्वयं विभुः॥२८॥

vavarṣa puṣpairanyonyaṁ viṣṇurviṣṇupriyā ca sā|
sākṣādeva mahānando'vatatāra svayaṁ vibhuḥ||28||

vavarsha — showered; pushpaih — with flowers; anyonyam — each other; vishnuh — Vishnu; vishnupriya — Vishnupriya; cha — and; sa — she; sakshat — visibly; eva — indeed; maha-anandah — Great Bliss; avatatara — descended; svayam — Himself; vibhuh — the Almighty.

28Vishnu and Vishnupriya showered each other with flowers: Great Bliss itself, the Almighty Himself, had visibly descended.

Verse 29

ततः स आसने शुभ्रे शुद्धास्तरणसंयुते।
उपविष्टो महाबाहुर्हरिः सा च शुभा वधूः॥२९॥

tataḥ sa āsane śubhre śuddhāstaraṇasaṁyute|
upaviṣṭo mahābāhurhariḥ sā ca śubhā vadhūḥ||29||

tatah — then; sah — He; asane — on a seat; shubhre — bright; shuddha-astarana-samyute — spread with a clean cloth; upavishtah — sat; maha-bahuh — mighty-armed; harih — Hari; sa — she; cha — and; shubha — lovely; vadhuh — bride.

29Then mighty-armed Hari sat on a bright seat spread with a clean cloth, and beside Him the lovely bride,

Verse 30

द्वारवत्यां यथा कृष्णो रुक्मिणी रुचिरानना।
ववृधेऽथानयोः कान्ती रोहिणीशशिनोरिव॥३०॥

dvāravatyāṁ yathā kṛṣṇo rukmiṇī rucirānanā|
vavṛdhe'thānayoḥ kāntī rohiṇīśaśinoriva||30||

dvaravatyam — in Dvaravati (Dvaraka); yatha — as; krishnah — Krishna; rukmini — Rukmini; ruchira-anana — of lovely face; vavridhe — grew; atha — and; anayoh — of the two; kanti — the radiance; rohini-shashinoh — of Rohini and the moon; iva — like.

30like Krishna in Dvaravati with fair-faced Rukmini, and their radiance grew like that of the moon and Rohini6.

Verse 31

आगत्य विधिवत्कन्यामुत्सृज्य करपङ्कजे।
दत्त्वा कृतार्थमात्मानं मेने स श्रीसनातनः॥३१॥

āgatya vidhivatkanyāmutsṛjya karapaṅkaje|
dattvā kṛtārthamātmānaṁ mene sa śrīsanātanaḥ||31||

agatya — approaching; vidhivat — according to the rite; kanyam — his daughter; utsrijya — giving away; kara-pankaje — into the lotus hand; dattva — having given; krita-artham — fulfilled; atmanam — himself; mene — considered; sah — he; shri-sanatanah — Sri Sanatana.

31Sri Sanatana came forward, gave his daughter's hand into the lotus hand (of the Lord) according to the rite, and, having given her away, considered his life fulfilled.

Verse 32

ततो विवाहे निर्वृत्ते कृत्वा च सुमहोत्सवम्।
आजगाम निजं गेहं सभार्यो जगतां गुरुः॥३२॥

tato vivāhe nirvṛtte kṛtvā ca sumahotsavam|
ājagāma nijaṁ gehaṁ sabhāryo jagatāṁ guruḥ||32||

tatah — then; vivahe nirvritte — when the wedding was complete; kritva — having held; cha — and; su-maha-utsavam — a very great festival; ajagama — came; nijam — to His own; geham — house; sa-bharyah — with His wife; jagatam — of the worlds; guruh — the Teacher.

32When the wedding was complete and a great festival had been held, the Teacher of the worlds returned with His wife to His own house.

Verse 33

दृष्ट्वा तु तं क्षितिसुरैरभिनन्द्यमानं
वध्वा समं सपदि गेहमुपागतं सा।
गेहप्रवेशनविधिं मुदिता चकार
साध्वीभिर्बन्धुरमुखी जननी मुरारेः॥३३॥

dṛṣṭvā tu taṁ kṣitisurairabhinandyamānaṁ
vadhvā samaṁ sapadi gehamupāgataṁ sā|
gehapraveśanavidhiṁ muditā cakāra
sādhvībhirbandhuramukhī jananī murāreḥ||33||

drishtva — seeing; tu — and; tam — Him; kshiti-suraih — by the gods on earth (brahmanas); abhinandyamanam — being greeted; vadhva samam — together with the bride; sapadi — soon; geham — to the house; upagatam — come; sa — she; geha-praveshana-vidhim — the rite of entering the house; mudita — joyful; chakara — performed; sadhvibhih — with virtuous women; bandhura-mukhi — lovely-faced; janani — the mother; murareh — of Murari (Krishna).

33Seeing Him soon arrive home with the bride, greeted by the gods on earth7, the lovely-faced mother of Murari8 joyfully performed, with the virtuous women, the rite of entering the house.

Thus ends the fourteenth sarga, "The Marriage of Sri Vishnupriya" (Shri-vishnupriya-vivaha), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The lagna is the zodiacal sign rising at the moment of the rite; a nakshatra is a lunar asterism. Their favourable conjunction with the moon determines the time of the wedding.
  2. Betel (tambula): betel leaves with areca nut and spices, offered to guests.
  3. The nandimukha are forefathers honoured with a special rite (nandimukha shraddha) before a wedding and other joyful occasions.
  4. Literally, "with a gracious face."
  5. Nirmanchhana: the rite of waving lamps and other auspicious things around the bridegroom to ward off the evil eye.
  6. Rohini is the nakshatra who is the favourite consort of the moon-god.
  7. The gods on earth are the brahmanas.
  8. Murari ("Enemy of Mura") is Krishna; here, Gauranga.
